captions.text: Imagine finding a matching value in an illustrative table. A table scan tests candidate rows against the search condition.
Without a useful index, the scan can examine many rows before finding a match.
An index instead maps a search key to matching rows, so the lookup need not test every row.
That shortcut has a trade-off: the index needs storage and updates when indexed values change.
The illustrative data are negative -12 units, zero 0 units and large 1500 units. These synthetic values test a zero-inclusive linear scale, not a benchmark or measurements.
